$comment: THE ONE PRECEDENCE FOR A PERSON'S NAME, WRITTEN ONCE AND ASSERTED EVERYWHERE.
Four implementations build a human name out of the three name columns of the `users` table -
one in chat-delivery-service, one in social-service, one in the frontend, and the initials
helper beside the last. Until 2026-09-22 the servers preferred `displayName` and the client
preferred `firstName lastName`, so the same account could be titled one way in a push
notification and another way in the screen it opened (backlog G2, reported by the user on
2026-09-18). There is no shared TypeScript package between the four - the apps are standalone
and the frontend is a separate build - so the CONTRACT is shared instead of the code: this file
is read by one spec per implementation, and a fifth implementation that does not read it is a
fifth implementation nobody is asserting.
THE PRECEDENCE IS `firstName lastName` FIRST, and the reason is that the pair is the STRUCTURED
identity: the initials helper, the trombinoscope's sort and the `firstNameOnly` chat label are
all derived from it, so preferring anything else names a person one way and abbreviates them
another. `displayName` is Authentik's free-form `name` claim, kept as the fallback for an
account whose parts never arrived.
`expected: null` means the row carries no name at all. Each implementation supplies its OWN
answer for that case - a localized label on the client, the raw id on a server that must return
something addressable, an empty string where the caller treats the name as decoration - and this
file deliberately does not pin it.
Every value is trimmed before it is considered, so a column holding only whitespace is absent.

cases.name: both parts present - they win over a display name
both parts present, no display name
no parts at all - the display name is the fallback
the parts are trimmed, and joined by exactly one space
a display name of whitespace is absent too
